symbols.name: G
symbols.def: Known undirected graph supplied to the full-neighborhood exposure mapping.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: Target exposure attained when a unit's whole block is treated.

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: Target exposure attained when a unit's whole block is controlled, with \(b\ne a\).

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Non-target label for a block containing both assignments.

symbols.name: e
symbols.def: Known exposure map induced by \(B\), and the reference map against which the \(R\) interference-package output is audited.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: Array \(Y=(Y_i(d):i\in U,d\in E)\) of finite-population potential outcomes.

symbols.name: mu
symbols.def: Latent block target means constructed in \(\mathrm{def{:}block\text{-}means}\).

symbols.name: ybarobs
symbols.def: Observed-data-measurable block means \(\overline Y_l^{\mathrm{obs}}(D)\) constructed in \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}block\text{-}means}\).

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: Indicators \(A_l=\mathbf 1\{Z_i=1\text{ for all }i\in B_l\}\), measurable from \(D\).

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: Indicators \(C_l=\mathbf 1\{Z_i=0\text{ for all }i\in B_l\}\), measurable from \(D\).

symbols.name: R
symbols.def: Auxiliary \(R\sim\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\) independent of the assignment and fixed schedule.

symbols.name: delta
symbols.def: Coordinate perturbation \(\delta=(\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_L)\) in the finite confidence-modulus program.

symbols.name: lambda
symbols.def: Multiplier \(\lambda_\alpha\) used by the capped water-filling algorithm.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: Independent reveal indicators \(K_l\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_l)\) in the hard subexperiment.

symbols.name: V
symbols.def: Latent block-homogeneous target outcomes in the weighted-erasure subexperiment.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: Index of the tilted product prior on the latent signs.

symbols.name: mathcalTtilt
symbols.def: Set \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{tilt}}=[-\|s\|_\infty^{-1},\|s\|_\infty^{-1}]\). The normalization \(\sum_{l=1}^Lq_ls_l^2=1\) ensures \(\|s\|_\infty>0\), so this is a finite compact interval.

symbols.name: Lambda
symbols.def: Generic measurable interval-valued rule in the lower experiment.

symbols.name: v
symbols.def: Generic fixed realization \(v=(v_1,\ldots,v_L)\) of the latent block signs.

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: A fixed Borel map whose pushforward of Lebesgue measure is product Lebesgue measure.

symbols.name: LambdaGamma
symbols.type: interval rule induced by an original-data rule

symbols.name: epkg
symbols.def: The deterministic map implemented by \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\), function \(\texttt{make\_exposure\_map\_full\_neighborhood}\), constructed in \(\mathrm{def{:}package\text{-}label\text{-}maps}\).

symbols.name: eref
symbols.def: Target unanimous-block label map constructed independently in \(\mathrm{def{:}package\text{-}label\text{-}maps}\).

symbols.name: lpkg

symbols.name: lref

standard.name: known partial-interference partition with unequal blocks

assumptions.condition: \(e_i(z)=a\iff z_j=1\ \forall j\in B_l,\quad e_i(z)=b\iff z_j=0\ \forall j\in B_l,\quad e_i(z)=m\text{ otherwise},\quad i\in B_l\).

standard.name: full-neighborhood exposure mapping on disjoint cliques
uniformly bounded fixed potential outcomes, centered variant

definitions.name: Uniformly randomization-valid interval procedures
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak C_\alpha=\{\Gamma:\inf_{m\in\mathcal M_n(B)}P_{Z,R,m}\{\theta(m)\in\Gamma(D,R)\}\ge1-\alpha\}\), where \(R\) may be unused and is independent of \(Z\).

definitions.name: Trimmed inverse-probability radius
definitions.construction: \(\rho_\alpha(w,q)=\inf_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,L\}}[\sum_{l\notin J}w_l+\sqrt{\log(2/\alpha)\sum_{l\in J}w_l^2/q_l}+\{\log(2/\alpha)/3\}\max_{l\in J}w_l/q_l]\), with the maximum over \(J=\varnothing\) equal to zero, and \(\rho_0(w,q)=\inf_J[\sum_{l\notin J}w_l+(\sum_{l\in J}w_l^2/q_l)^{1/2}]\).

definitions.name: Finite capped confidence modulus and water-filling certificate
definitions.construction: \(\omega_\alpha(w,q)=\max\{\sum_{l=1}^Lw_l\delta_l:0\le\delta_l\le1\ \forall l,\ \sum_{l=1}^Lq_l\delta_l^2\le x_\alpha\}\). If \(x_\alpha\ge\sum_lq_l\), set \(\delta_l^*=1\) for every \(l\). Otherwise choose the unique \(\lambda_\alpha>0\) solving \(\sum_lq_l\min\{1,\lambda_\alpha w_l/q_l\}^2=x_\alpha\), and set \(\delta_l^*=\min\{1,\lambda_\alpha w_l/q_l\}\). Sorting the breakpoints \(q_l/w_l\) and solving the displayed scalar equation on each adjacent interval is the finite water-filling algorithm.

definitions.name: Explicit tilted product prior and induced target
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{tilt}}=[-\|s\|_\infty^{-1},\|s\|_\infty^{-1}]\). For each \(t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{tilt}}\), \(\pi_t=\bigotimes_{l=1}^L\pi_{t,l}\), where \(\pi_{t,l}\{V_l=1/2\}=(1+ts_l)/2\) and \(\pi_{t,l}\{V_l=-1/2\}=(1-ts_l)/2\). Hence every coordinate probability lies in \([0,1]\), and the induced target functional is \(\tau_t=\mathbb E_{\pi_t}[T(V)]=(t/2)\sum_{l=1}^Lw_ls_l=t\sqrt S/2\).

definitions.name: Independent weighted-erasure experiment
definitions.construction: \(P_K=\bigotimes_{l=1}^L\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_l)\), \(O=((K_l,K_lV_l))_{l=1}^L\), and \(Q_t=\pi_t\otimes P_K\otimes\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\) on \((V,K,R)\). Thus \(K\) is independent of \(V\), and the external randomizer \(R\) is independent of \((V,K)\), under every \(Q_t\).

definitions.name: Hard-subexperiment schedule, ancillary reconstruction, and interval reduction
definitions.construction:
For \(v=(v_1,\ldots,v_L)\in\{-1/2,1/2\}^L\), define \(m_v\) by \(Y_i^v(d)=v_l\) if \(i\in B_l\) and \(d=a\), and \(Y_i^v(d)=0\) if \(i\in B_l\) and \(d
e a\). Put \(K_l=A_l\). Let \(
u_{l,1}=\delta_{\mathbf 1_{B_l}}\) and \(
u_{l,0}=\operatorname{Uniform}(\{0,1\}^{B_l}\setminus\{\mathbf 1_{B_l}\})\). Fix a Borel measure-preserving \( eta:[0,1]	o[0,1]^{L+1}\), write \( eta(R)=(R_0,R_1,\ldots,R_L)\), and choose measurable \(F_l\) such that \(F_l(k_l,R_l)\sim
u_{l,k_l}\). Set \(Z^*_{B_l}=F_l(K_l,R_l)\), \(Y_i^*=K_lV_l\) for \(i\in B_l\), and \(D^*=(Z^*,Y^*)\). For every measurable \(\Gamma\), define \(\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)=\Gamma(D^*(O,R_1,\ldots,R_L),R_0)\).

definitions.name: Heterogeneous weighted-erasure posterior-spread handle
definitions.construction: Start from the explicit family \((Q_t:t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{tilt}})\), use the separation \(\tau_t=t\sqrt S/2\), control random weighted information and the two posterior tails of \(T(V)\) conditional on \(O\), and apply an interval-coverage averaging inequality to \(\Lambda(O,R)\) under the same joint laws.

definitions.name: Capped perturbation and trimming duality handle
definitions.construction: Use the explicit optimizer \(\delta_l^*=\min\{1,\lambda_\alpha w_l/q_l\}\) to build a block-homogeneous weighted-erasure testing family, prove bounded pairwise divergence from \(\sum_lq_l(\delta_l^*)^2\le x_\alpha\), and dualize its target separation against the subset-trimmed radius \(\rho_\alpha(w,q)\).

definitions.name: Pinned package and independent reference label maps
definitions.construction: For the explicit domain \(\{G\in\{0,1\}^{U\times U}:G=G^\top,\ G_{ii}=0\ \forall i\in U\}\), let \(N_G[i]=\{i\}\cup\{j:G_{ij}=1\}\). The deterministic map implemented by \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\), function \(\texttt{make\_exposure\_map\_full\_neighborhood}\), sends this graph domain and \(\{0,1\}^U\) into \(\{0,1\}^{U\times\{a,b\}}\), with \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{pkg},i,a}^{0.1.0}(G,z)=\mathbf 1\{\sum_{j\in N_G[i]}z_j=|N_G[i]|\}\) and \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{pkg},i,b}^{0.1.0}(G,z)=\mathbf 1\{\sum_{j\in N_G[i]}z_j<|N_G[i]|\}\). Independently define \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{ref}}:(B,z)\mapsto\{0,1\}^{U\times\{a,b\}}\) by \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{ref},i,a}(B,z)=\mathbf 1\{z_j=1\ \forall j\in B_l\}\) and \(\mathsf E_{\mathrm{ref},i,b}(B,z)=\mathbf 1\{z_j=0\ \forall j\in B_l\}\) for the unique \(l\) with \(i\in B_l\). The external and reference outputs supplied to the diagnostic are \(L^{\mathrm{pkg}}=\mathsf E_{\mathrm{pkg}}^{0.1.0}(G,Z)\) and \(L^{\mathrm{ref}}=\mathsf E_{\mathrm{ref}}(B,Z)\), respectively.

definitions.name: Auditable full-neighborhood exposure diagnostic for \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\)
definitions.construction: \(\Phi(G,B,D,\alpha,L^{\mathrm{pkg}},L^{\mathrm{ref}})\) takes both the externally returned output of \(\texttt{make\_exposure\_map\_full\_neighborhood}\) and the independently recomputed target labels. It first checks \(N_G[i]=B_l\) for every \(i\in B_l\). Failure of this graph check returns \(\texttt{graph-reject}\) with the first crossing neighborhood or nonclique witness; this is the branch for overlapping-neighborhood inputs. On a valid unequal-clique graph, it checks \(L^{\mathrm{pkg}}=\mathsf E_{\mathrm{pkg}}^{0.1.0}(G,Z)\), \(L^{\mathrm{ref}}=\mathsf E_{\mathrm{ref}}(B,Z)\), and then the coordinatewise equality \(L^{\mathrm{pkg}}=L^{\mathrm{ref}}\). Any failed equality returns \(\texttt{label-mismatch}\) and the first unequal coordinate. Only after all checks pass does \(\Phi\) compute \(\overline Y_l^{\mathrm{obs}}(D)\) and return \((r_l,q_l,w_l,A_l,C_l)_{l=1}^L\), \(S\), \(M\), \(\omega_\alpha\), \(\rho_\alpha\), and \(I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha}(D)\); both rejection branches suppress the confidence output.

statements.statement: For every \(m\in\mathcal M_n(B)\), \(\overline Y_l^{\mathrm{obs}}(D)\) is measurable with respect to \(D\), and \(A_l=1\) implies \(\overline Y_l^{\mathrm{obs}}(D)=\mu_l(a)\), while \(C_l=1\) implies \(\overline Y_l^{\mathrm{obs}}(D)=\mu_l(b)\).
statements.justification: This measurability bridge licenses every occurrence of the fixed-schedule block target mean in the expectation calculation without placing it inside the reported statistic.
statements.gap: Exposure-weighted estimators are standard, but the clique reduction requires an explicit observed-data equality on each mutually exclusive unanimous event.
statements.consumer: The block estimator, clipped interval, and software diagnostic consume only assignment and observed outcomes.

statements.statement: For every \(m\in\mathcal M_n(B)\), the vectors \((A_l,C_l,H_l)\) are independent across \(l\), each has categorical probabilities \((q_l,q_l,1-2q_l)\), and \(A_lC_l=0\). The observed-data construction in \(\mathrm{def{:}block\text{-}ht}\) satisfies \(\mathbb E_Z[X_l(D)]=w_l\{\mu_l(a)-\mu_l(b)\}\), \(\sum_l\operatorname{Var}_Z\{X_l(D)\}\le S/2\), and \(|X_l(D)-\mathbb E_ZX_l(D)|\le w_l/q_l\le M\).
statements.justification: The exact categorical reduction preserves mutual exclusion and supplies the heterogeneous variance and increment scales for an implementable statistic.
statements.gap: AronowSamii2017 gives general exposure-probability Horvitz--Thompson algebra, while UganderKarrerBackstromKleinberg2013 studies full-neighborhood exposure; neither isolates this independent nonidentical weighted-erasure experiment.
statements.consumer: The upper interval, lower prior, and package diagnostic use the same exact block law and do not approximate dependence within blocks.

statements.statement: For every \(0<\alpha\le1/4\) and every \(m\in\mathcal M_n(B)\), the interval \(I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha}(D)\), which is a measurable function solely of \(D\) and known design quantities, obeys \(P_{Z,m}\{\theta\in I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha}(D)\}\ge1-\alpha\) and \(\operatorname{len}\{I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha}(D)\}\le2\min\{1,\sqrt{S\log(2/\alpha)}+(M/3)\log(2/\alpha)\}\).
statements.justification: This is a genuinely reportable finite-sample interval: no latent block mean appears in the statistic or its endpoints.
statements.gap: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012, Section 4.3, gives Hoeffding intervals for four binary two-stage partial-interference effects, and RigdonHudgens2015 inverts randomization tests for those effects under stratified interference. Their designs and estimands differ from the observed-data All Treat versus All Control interval under fixed independent assignment on unequal cliques.
statements.consumer: An analyst using full-neighborhood exposures obtains a computable finite-sample interval and sees when a single rare block controls length.

statements.statement:
For every \(v=(v_1,\ldots,v_L)\in\{-1/2,1/2\}^L\), the fixed block-homogeneous schedule \(m_v\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}hard	ext{-}subexperiment	ext{-}embedding}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_n(B)\), because it is fixed and all outcomes lie in \([-1/2,1/2]\); moreover, \(\mu_l^v(a)=v_l\), \(\mu_l^v(b)=0\), and \(	heta(m_v)=\sum_{l=1}^Lw_lv_l=T(v)\). Under \(m_v\), \(K_l=A_l=\mathbf 1\{Z_{B_l}=\mathbf 1_{B_l}\}\), the \(K_l\) are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_l)\), \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=K_lv_l\) for \(i\in B_l\), and \(O_l=(K_l,K_lv_l)\) is measurable from \(D\). The remaining assignment information is retained exactly: \(\operatorname{Law}(Z\mid K=k)= igotimes_{l=1}^L
u_{l,k_l}\), where \(
u_{l,1}=\delta_{\mathbf 1_{B_l}}\) and \(
u_{l,0}=\operatorname{Uniform}(\{0,1\}^{B_l}\setminus\{\mathbf 1_{B_l}\})\), so the \(K_l=0\) branch includes all-control and every mixed pattern with their original conditional probabilities. With the measure-preserving splitter \( eta(R)=(R_0,R_1,\ldots,R_L)\), the samplers \(F_l\), and \(D^*\) of the same definition, \(\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)=\Gamma(D^*(O,R_1,\ldots,R_L),R_0)\) is measurable in \((O,R)\) for every measurable externally randomized \(\Gamma\). For every fixed \(v\), \[\operatorname{Law}(D^*,R_0\mid V=v)=\operatorname{Law}_{Z,R_0,m_v}(D,R_0),\] and therefore \[P_{K,R}\{T(v)\in\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\mid V=v\}=P_{Z,R_0,m_v}\{	heta(m_v)\in\Gamma(D,R_0)\},\qquad \mathbb E_{K,R}[\operatorname{len}\{\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\}\mid V=v]=\mathbb E_{Z,R_0,m_v}[\operatorname{len}\{\Gamma(D,R_0)\}].\] Consequently, if \(\Gamma\in\mathfrak C_\alpha\), then \(\Lambda_\Gamma\) has coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) for every fixed \(v\), \(Q_t\{T(V)\in\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{tilt}}\), and \[\sup_{m'\in\mathcal M_n(B)}\mathbb E_{Z,R,m'}[\operatorname{len}\{\Gamma(D,R)\}]\ge\sup_{v\in\{-1/2,1/2\}^L}\mathbb E_{K,R}[\operatorname{len}\{\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\}\mid V=v]\ge\mathbb E_{Q_t}[\operatorname{len}\{\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\}]\] for every admissible \(t\). Taking the supremum over admissible \(t\), applying a weighted-erasure spread result if and when it is proved, and then taking the infimum over \(\Gamma\in\mathfrak C_\alpha\) yields the minimax lower bound. Thus the bridge preserves the entire randomized decision experiment; it does not assert the weighted-erasure posterior-spread inequality.
statements.justification: This exact Markov-kernel embedding retains every assignment ancillary and transfers pointwise coverage and expected length for arbitrary externally randomized original-data intervals.
statements.gap: The weighted-erasure lower experiment is not automatically a subexperiment for arbitrary procedures unless the unrevealed assignment patterns and external randomization are reconstructed with their exact laws.
statements.consumer: The posterior-spread question and no-dominance minimax theorem can invoke a rigorous experiment-to-experiment reduction without assuming ancillary irrelevance.

statements.statement: Establish or refute the following assertion using \(H_{\mathrm{WE}}\). There exist universal \(c_0,c_1,c_2\in(0,1)\) such that, for every \(0<\alpha\le1/4\) and every \((w,q)\) satisfying \(\sum_{l=1}^Lq_ls_l^2=1\) and \(\|s\|_\infty\sqrt{x_\alpha}\le c_0\), the interval \([-c_2\sqrt{x_\alpha},c_2\sqrt{x_\alpha}]\) is contained in \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{tilt}}\), and every measurable \(\Lambda(O,R)\) obeys \[\inf_{|t|\le c_2\sqrt{x_\alpha}}Q_t\{T(V)\in\Lambda(O,R)\}\ge1-\alpha\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\sup_{|t|\le c_2\sqrt{x_\alpha}}\mathbb E_{Q_t}[\operatorname{len}\{\Lambda(O,R)\}]\ge c_1\min\{1,\sqrt{Sx_\alpha}\}.\] Here \(Q_t=\pi_t\otimes P_K\otimes\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\): every probability and expectation integrates \(V\sim\pi_t\), \(K\sim P_K\) independently of \(V\), and the external \(R\) independently of \((V,K)\). The assertion is solely the posterior-spread inequality. The pointwise-coverage and worst-case-to-prior-average transfer for \(\Lambda_\Gamma\) is supplied by \(\mathrm{lem{:}hard\text{-}subexperiment\text{-}embedding}\), not assumed here.
statements.justification: The fully specified prior family and joint law make the first-class lower-bound bottleneck falsifiable for centered, uncentered, deterministic, and externally randomized intervals.
statements.gap: CaiLow2004 and ArmstrongKolesar2018 obtain modulus lower bounds in Gaussian experiments, while FelixGarciaSousa2025 treats one-parameter discrete families; none proves posterior spread for a weighted nonidentical erasure experiment with compact block outcomes.
statements.consumer: A successful lemma certifies rate optimality among all honest procedures, not only inverse-probability or nonrandomized intervals.

statements.statement: There exist universal constants \(c_0,c_1,C_1>0\) such that, for every \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), \(M\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}\le c_0\sqrt S\) implies \[c_1\min\{1,\sqrt{S\log(1/\alpha)}\}\le\mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\le C_1\min\{1,\sqrt{S\log(1/\alpha)}\}.\] The infimum defining \(\mathcal R_\alpha\) includes every measurable procedure randomized by \(R\).
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: the confidence-sensitive minimax frontier is characterized over heterogeneous fixed schedules.
statements.gap: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012 and RigdonHudgens2015 provide finite two-stage partial-interference intervals for specified binary-effect procedures but no all-procedure expected-length lower bound. The equal-block analysis has one reveal probability and an extreme-confidence cutoff, while KandirosHarshawSavje2026 characterizes mean-squared-error rates with design and estimator as decision variables.
statements.consumer: The result supplies a precision benchmark for school, village, and online-network partitions whose component sizes and exposure probabilities vary.

statements.statement: For every \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), there exists an interval in \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\), measurable from \(D\), obtained by minimizing over \(J\), applying the observed-data block Horvitz--Thompson estimator on \(J\), and adding omitted contrast allowance \(\sum_{l\notin J}w_l\), whose length is at most \(2\min\{1,\rho_\alpha(w,q)\}\).
statements.justification: Trimming prevents a low-weight, astronomically rare block from making the global interval inconsistent through inverse-probability amplification.
statements.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026 removes difficult conflict-graph vertices for mean-squared error; this fixed-design procedure protects omitted causal contrast and retains finite-sample coverage.
statements.consumer: The interval tells practitioners when to bias-protect a negligible rare block rather than report an explosive inverse-probability radius.

statements.statement: Using \(H_{\mathrm{WF}}\), establish or refute universal constants \(c,C>0\) such that, without a dominance restriction, \[c\min\{1,\omega_\alpha(w,q)\}\le\mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\le C\min\{1,\omega_\alpha(w,q)\},\qquad C^{-1}\omega_\alpha(w,q)\le\rho_\alpha(w,q)\le C\omega_\alpha(w,q).\] The proof must certify the explicit capped optimizer and its trimming dual, including all-measurable externally randomized intervals. When no cap binds, it must give \(\omega_\alpha=\sqrt{S\log(1/\alpha)}\).
statements.justification: Outside the Lindeberg regime, the explicit finite program makes the dominance-aware claim falsifiable rather than naming an unspecified modulus.
statements.gap: BasseAiroldi2018 gives a nonconcentration warning and KandirosHarshawSavje2026 gives graph-subset MSE bounds; neither derives an exact confidence-dependent weighted-clique water-filling program.
statements.consumer: The optimizer identifies blocks that remain quadratic, hit their outcome cap, or should be protected by trimming.

statements.statement: For the unequal six-block population with \(r=(1,1,1,3,3,3)\), \(n=12\), and \(\alpha=1/4\), the three size-three coordinates cap and the three size-one coordinates do not. Explicitly, \(\lambda_\alpha=\sqrt{24(\log4-3/8)}\), \(\omega_{1/4}=3/4+\sqrt{(\log4-3/8)/24}\approx0.9553\), and the subset retaining only size-one blocks gives \(\rho_0\le3/4+1/\sqrt{24}\approx0.9541\).
statements.justification: The numerical exhibit exposes the cap threshold and the near-matching trimming certificate in a reproducible unequal-block instance.
statements.gap: An equal-block substitution has only one breakpoint and therefore cannot reproduce simultaneous capped and uncapped coordinates.
statements.consumer: The software diagnostic uses this instance as a unit test for sorting, multiplier solution, and trimming output.

statements.statement: For every triangular array \((B^{(n)},w^{(n)},q^{(n)})\) and every fixed \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), \[\mathcal R_\alpha(w^{(n)},q^{(n)})\to0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\omega_\alpha(w^{(n)},q^{(n)})\to0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\rho_0(w^{(n)},q^{(n)})\to0.\] In particular, \(S^{(n)}\to0\) is sufficient but not necessary.
statements.justification: The if-and-only-if boundary replaces the misleading requirement that untrimmed Horvitz--Thompson variance vanish.
statements.gap: BasseAiroldi2018 gives an impossibility warning and UganderYin2023 mitigates small probabilities by changing design; neither characterizes consistency for this fixed unequal-block experiment.
statements.consumer: Designers can separate intrinsically uninformative experiments from those destabilized only by negligible inverse-probability coordinates.

statements.statement: Let \(B^{(k)}\) contain \(k\) blocks of size two and \(k\) blocks of size four, so \(n=6k\). Then the two strata have \((w_l,q_l)=(1/(3k),1/4)\) and \((2/(3k),1/16)\), respectively, \(S=68/(9k)\), and \(M=32/(3k)\). For fixed \(\alpha\), the dominance ratio is \(32\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}/\sqrt{68k}\to0\), and \(\mathrm{thm{:}no\text{-}dominance\text{-}frontier}\) predicts minimax length of order \(\sqrt{68\log(1/\alpha)/(9k)}\). No common block size \(r\) can reproduce both reveal probabilities \(1/4\) and \(1/16\) or the two water-filling breakpoint values.
statements.justification: This concrete triangular array makes the heterogeneous theorem refutable through exact constants and a nondegenerate two-scale exposure structure.
statements.gap: The inherited equal-block formula collapses all blocks to one reveal probability and one cap threshold, so it cannot deliver this two-stratum prediction.
statements.consumer: A simulation study and the package diagnostic can check the predicted \(k^{-1/2}\) confidence-length curve separately within the two exposure strata.

statements.statement: As an inherited sanity corollary, if \(r_l=r\) for every \(l\), then \(L=n/r\), \(q_l=2^{-r}\), \(w_l=r/n\), and \(S=M=r2^r/n\). The no-dominance condition becomes \(r2^r\log(1/\alpha)/n\le c_0^2\), and the resulting length order is \(\sqrt{r2^r\log(1/\alpha)/n}\) for every \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), without an extreme-confidence cutoff.
statements.justification: This is solely a reduction check showing that the heterogeneous formulas contain the established equal-block effective-count calculation.
statements.gap: No independent novelty is claimed for the equal-block identity; the contribution begins when weights, reveal probabilities, and cap thresholds differ.
statements.consumer: Users with regular partitions recover the familiar \(n/(r2^r)\) effective count as a check on the general implementation.

statements.statement: Let \(L^{\mathrm{pkg}}=\mathsf E_{\mathrm{pkg}}^{0.1.0}(G,Z)\) be the labels externally returned by \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\), function \(\texttt{make\_exposure\_map\_full\_neighborhood}\), and let \(L^{\mathrm{ref}}=\mathsf E_{\mathrm{ref}}(B,Z)\) be independently recomputed. If \(G\) is the disjoint union of the unequal clique components \(B_1,\ldots,B_L\), then \[L^{\mathrm{pkg}}=L^{\mathrm{ref}}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A_l+C_l=1\text{ for every }l.\] In particular, because the pinned package map labels its second column by the complement of All Treat, a mixed block produces an explicit second-column mismatch with the target All Control map. On a valid clique input, \(\Phi(G,B,D,\alpha,L^{\mathrm{pkg}},L^{\mathrm{ref}})\) returns \(\texttt{label-equal}\) and the exact \(q_l=2^{-r_l}\), observed unanimous-block statistics, \(S\), \(M\), \(\omega_\alpha\), \(\rho_\alpha\), and \(I_{\mathrm{HT},\alpha}(D)\) exactly when the displayed equality holds; otherwise it returns \(\texttt{label-mismatch}\) with a coordinate witness and no interval. If any \(N_G[i]\ne B_l\) for \(i\in B_l\), including overlapping-neighborhood or nonclique inputs, it instead returns \(\texttt{graph-reject}\) with a structural witness before performing the label equality check and produces no interval.
statements.justification: The proposition makes the software claim a reproducible equality test against a pinned implementation and separates graph-domain rejection from assignment-dependent label disagreement.
statements.gap: AronowEcklesSamiiZonszein2021 demonstrates the \(R\) exposure workflow, but its companion package interface does not certify that the returned two-column labels equal the target unanimous All Treat and All Control map on each realized assignment.
statements.consumer: A package user receives either a certified exact rare-exposure interval, a concrete package-versus-reference coordinate mismatch, or a distinct structural rejection for an overlapping or nonclique graph.

sampling_model.design: Known independent unit-level \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment on a fixed partition into unequal disjoint cliques.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) units, partition, graph, exposure map, and all exposure-indexed potential outcomes are fixed.
sampling_model.treatment: Within block \(l\), All Treat and All Control are mutually exclusive events, each with probability \(q_l=2^{-r_l}\); blocks are independent.
sampling_model.overlap: Every target exposure has known positive probability \(q_l\), which may vary with \(l\) and vanish along triangular arrays.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No superpopulation nuisance is estimated; on a unanimous block, the observed block mean equals the corresponding fixed-schedule block mean, and omitted blocks receive deterministic bias protection.
sampling_model.randomness: The only inferential randomness is \(Z\), augmented by independent \(R\) solely to include externally randomized interval procedures in the decision class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Exposure-weighted estimators are unbiased, conservative randomization variances are available, and local-dependence conditions justify asymptotic normal intervals.

Section 4.3 constructs finite-sample Hoeffding-type confidence intervals for population-average direct, indirect, total, and overall effects of binary outcomes under a two-stage partial-interference design.

Exact confidence sets for binary direct, indirect, total, and overall effects under two-stage randomization and stratified partial interference are obtained by inversion of randomization tests, with a targeted approximation algorithm.
Full-neighborhood exposure probabilities can be exponentially small in degree and graph-cluster randomization can sharply reduce Horvitz--Thompson variance.
Conflict-graph connectivity controls upper and lower minimax mean-squared-error rates when the design and estimator are decision variables.
Under ordinary randomized experiments, nonasymptotic treatment-effect intervals attain the effective sample size \(n\pi\), with matching estimation-rate lower bounds.
Between-class moduli lower-bound expected confidence-interval length and ordered moduli yield procedures within constant factors in Gaussian models.
Convex regression classes admit finite-sample modulus-based optimal intervals and sharp efficiency bounds under normal errors with known variance.
Under interference, existence of unbiased estimators does not guarantee variance that decreases with population size.
Randomized fuzzy intervals attain a minimum expected-length benchmark for a one-parameter Bernoulli observation problem.

tldr: Unequal clique sizes turn full-neighborhood treatment and control exposure into independent nonidentical categorical reveals. The clipped Horvitz--Thompson interval is explicitly a function of \(D=(Z,Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\), and the field-level kernel is the all-randomized-interval \(\sqrt{S\log(1/\alpha)}\) converse under no dominance. A standalone hard-subexperiment lemma reconstructs every unrevealed assignment pattern with its exact conditional law, splits one uniform randomizer measurably, and preserves pointwise coverage and expected length for arbitrary randomized original-data intervals. The remaining open lower obligation is only the posterior-spread inequality under the explicit \(Q_t=\pi_t\otimes P_K\otimes\operatorname{Uniform}[0,1]\) laws. Existing finite partial-interference intervals concern two-stage allocation-strategy effects for binary outcomes, whereas this target is the All Treat versus All Control contrast under fixed independent assignment on unequal cliques. Globally, the capped program \(\omega_\alpha\), its water-filling optimizer, and trimmed dual remain an open dominance-aware frontier. The pinned \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\) diagnostic separately reports graph rejection and package-versus-reference label mismatch; the equal-block formula is only an inherited sanity corollary.

project_justification.gap: Tchetgen Tchetgen--VanderWeele Section 4.3 gives Hoeffding-type finite-sample intervals for direct, indirect, total, and overall binary-outcome effects under two-stage partial interference, and Rigdon--Hudgens gives exact randomization-test inversions for those effects under stratified interference. Exposure-mapping papers give inverse weighting and asymptotic inference, while recent network minimax theory studies mean-squared error and often chooses the design. None treats fixed independent assignment on unequal cliques as a heterogeneous categorical erasure channel or lower-bounds the expected length of every uniformly valid randomized interval. The equal-block calculation cannot express simultaneous reveal probabilities, weights, or cap thresholds.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a confidence-length information frontier jointly determined by unequal block weights, exponentially varying reveal probabilities, mutually exclusive target exposures, bounded fixed outcomes, and optional external interval randomization. It is quadratic under no dominance and is the explicit capped water-filling program otherwise.
project_justification.fill: The paper derives an observed-data block statistic and clipped Bernstein interval, supplies an exact Markov-kernel embedding that retains unrevealed assignment ancillaries and external randomization, and isolates the falsifiable posterior-spread inequality under the tilted sign laws as the sole no-dominance lower-bound bottleneck. It asks separately for a global equivalence between minimax length, the finite capped program, and trimming. Exact two-scale and six-block exhibits make the heterogeneous and saturation claims checkable. The version-pinned package diagnostic compares externally returned and independently recomputed labels, distinguishes graph rejection from label mismatch, and returns an interval only after equality is certified; equal blocks serve only as a reduction check.

related_work: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012, Section 4.3, derives finite-sample Hoeffding-type confidence intervals for population-average direct, indirect, total, and overall effects with binary outcomes under a two-stage partial-interference design; those allocation-strategy estimands and martingale bounds inform the finite-sample objective but are not the fixed unequal-clique All Treat versus All Control estimand or an expected-length lower frontier. RigdonHudgens2015 assumes two-stage randomization, binary outcomes, partial interference, and stratified interference, then obtains exact confidence sets for the same four effect types by inverting sharp-null randomization tests and supplies a targeted approximation algorithm; it addresses procedural exactness rather than minimax length over all randomized intervals. AronowSamii2017 supplies the design--exposure--estimand architecture, exposure-specific inverse weighting, conservative variance analysis, and local-dependence normal approximation; these ingredients inform the observed block estimator. UganderKarrerBackstromKleinberg2013 defines full-neighborhood exposure and shows its probability may be exponentially small in degree; it motivates the rare categorical channel but does not characterize confidence length. BasseAiroldi2018 shows that design-unbiased inference under interference need not concentrate; the capped program targets an exact consistency boundary on the unequal-clique family. UganderYin2023 changes the clustering design to mitigate unlucky vertices, whereas the design here is fixed. KandirosPipisDaskalakisHarshaw2024 and KandirosHarshawSavje2026 use exposure conflict graphs for estimator control, asymptotic intervals, and design-based minimax mean-squared error; difficult-vertex removal informs trimming, but their criterion is not the confidence-dependent all-interval risk. CaiLow2004 and ArmstrongKolesar2018 inform the testing-modulus logic for honest expected-length lower bounds in Gaussian experiments; the weighted erasure likelihood, compact coordinate caps, and external randomization require a different lemma. SandovalEtAl2026 gives nonasymptotic effective-count intervals without interference and an estimation-risk converse. FelixGarciaSousa2025 shows why randomized procedures cannot simply be omitted in a discrete experiment. HarshawMiddletonSavje2021 informs later variance adaptivity, and AronowEcklesSamiiZonszein2021 supplies the practitioner workflow consumed by the diagnostic. The pinned \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\) source defines a two-column full-neighborhood map whose second column is the complement of All Treat; the diagnostic therefore compares its external output with an independently recomputed unanimous All Control reference rather than identifying the two by name. Every named theorem-level result is treated as informing rather than as an estimand-preserving extension. No independent novelty is attached to the equal-block identity; the contribution is falsified by the stated unequal two-scale family if its weighted-erasure frontier fails.
technical_internal_limitation: The hard-subexperiment lemma settles only the experiment-to-experiment bridge: it reconstructs unrevealed assignments and transfers coverage and expected length without discarding ancillaries. The weighted posterior-spread assertion remains the early kill test under the explicit laws \(Q_t\); it must jointly control random weighted information, compact-prior boundaries, unrevealed target slope, conditional target fluctuation, and external randomization for every \(0<\alpha\le1/4\). A counterexample with \(M\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}/\sqrt S\to0\) defeats the field-level kernel. Outside that regime, the displayed capped program is explicit, but its equivalence to minimax interval length and the trimmed radius remains an open-ended question rather than following from the upper bound.
honest_scope: The fixed design is independent balanced assignment on known unequal disjoint cliques, the estimand is the finite-population All Treat versus All Control contrast, and outcomes are fixed in \([-1/2,1/2]\). The observed interval uses only \(D\) and known design quantities. The exact hard-subexperiment embedding preserves all assignment ancillaries and arbitrary external interval randomization, but it does not prove posterior spread. The no-dominance converse depends on the explicitly posed \(Q_t\)-posterior-spread question, and unrestricted water-filling equivalence remains open. The finite intervals of Tchetgen Tchetgen--VanderWeele and Rigdon--Hudgens concern binary allocation-strategy effects under two-stage partial-interference designs and are not claimed as corollaries. Overlapping or nonclique neighborhoods are rejected by the software diagnostic. On valid unequal cliques, the pinned package output is checked against an independently recomputed target map and may fail on mixed assignments; no package-label equivalence is presumed. No claim is made for unknown exposure mappings, optimized designs, asymptotic normality, or variance adaptivity. Equal blocks recover \(S=M=r2^r/n\) only as a sanity reduction; the two-scale family supplies the non-equal test case.

literature_map.anchor: AronowSamii2017 supplies the exposure-specific inverse-weighting construction and design-based setup. TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012, Section 4.3, and RigdonHudgens2015 establish that finite-sample confidence intervals are available for binary direct, indirect, total, and overall effects in two-stage partial-interference designs. The kernel here uses an observed unanimous-block mean for a different fixed-design All Treat versus All Control estimand and adds an all-procedure confidence-length converse.

literature_map.writing_adaptation: The motivation moves from unobserved estimand-relevant schedules, to the lack of a precision benchmark, to a fixed-design information frontier, and then to an observed software output.
literature_map.method_adaptation: Exposure-specific inverse weighting yields the observed block estimator; exact block independence permits Bernstein concentration. The two-stage Hoeffding and permutation-inversion papers delimit existing finite partial-interference inference without supplying the present estimand or decision-theoretic lower bound. Gaussian confidence-modulus logic motivates the lower risk, and difficult-vertex removal motivates trimming. The explicitly tilted weighted-erasure likelihood and capped KKT program remain new proof obligations.
